descriptionChirho: The substantivized superlative adjective ὕψιστος used as a divine epithet, 'the Most High,' referring to God as supreme over all. Found in phrases like 'Son of the Most High' (Luke 1:32), 'power of the Most High' (Luke 1:35), and 'servants of the Most High God' (Acts 16:17). Translated uniformly as a divine title: Spanish 'Altísimo,' Arabic 'العلي,' Hindi 'परमप्रधान/सर्वोच्च,' Korean '지극히 높으신 이,' Swahili 'Aliye Juu.' The 9 occurrences in S78323 use genitive/nominative masculine singular forms.

The superlative adjective ὕψιστος in the dative neuter plural, functioning as a spatial/locative reference to 'the highest places' or 'the heights' of heaven, as in the angelic doxology 'Glory to God in the highest' (Luke 2:14, 19:38; Matt 21:9; Mark 11:10). Spanish renders this as 'las alturas/altísimos,' Arabic 'الأعالي,' Hindi 'सर्वोच्चों,' Korean '높은 곳들에,' Swahili 'juu sana.' This spatial/cosmic sense—the highest reaches of heaven—is semantically distinct from the personal divine title 'Most High' applied to God himself.
